etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle French retirer (“draw back”), from Old French retirer, built from re- (“back”) + tirer (“draw, pull”), the latter from Vulgar Latin *tīrāre, of highly uncertain origin.
senses: (intransitive) To stop working on a permanent basis, usually because of old age or illness.
(intransitive, sports) To stop playing their sport and in competitions a sports player.
(rare) The act of retiring, or the state of being retired.
A place to which one retires.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: (transitive, American spelling) To fit (a vehicle) with new tires.
